BLOCKER: AC5's required single conformance fixture set (valid + every RESIDENCY_* code incl. schema/invalid-field/toolchain/profile, identical pass/block from core.packaging.validate and cmd/pfresidency) is absent — only per-language tests exist; nothing pins cross-implementation parity per error code.

Go Validate never checks the egress group (no RESIDENCY_MISSING_GROUP:egress path) while Python does — the two authorities disagree on "all six groups"; a manifest without egress fails Python, passes Go, and trips the gate's parity path as an execution failure.

residency_gate.py returns `0 if a.report else 2` on validator-unavailable / no-JSON / parity failures — --report downgrades execution failures to pass, violating AC5 "warn only downgrades policy violations, never execution failures"; a broken Go toolchain silently passes CI.
MAJOR: `_policy()` swallows any residency-policy.json read error and defaults gate_mode to "warn" — unreadable/missing policy silently weakens the gate, contradicting the doc's "unreadable policy always blocks" and fail-closed intent.

Undetected parity divergences: Go lowercases backup.frequency before lookup, Python does not ("DAILY" passes Go, fails Python); Go checks kms.provider without TrimSpace, Python strips; backup MISSING_GROUP heuristics differ (all-zero struct vs empty dict). The gate compares only booleans, so code-set drift is invisible.

cmd/pfresidency exits 2 (stderr text, no JSON) for missing/unknown home via LoadProfile — a policy violation is misclassified as an execution failure and RESIDENCY_UNKNOWN_HOME never reaches a structured report, contrary to the frozen-code/report AC.

core/packaging.py implements the full policy engine (subsets, retention bound, frequency, provider) rather than a shape/home pre-check — a second source of truth for policy semantics shipped in Python, widening the language-rule exemption beyond "emit/validate the section".
MINOR: RESIDENCY_MANIFEST_UNREADABLE:{exception text} embeds volatile detail into the error code, breaking the "stable error codes" contract for reports, fixtures, and greps.
HOME_NOT_ALLOWED fires when home_region is merely missing (empty), conflating missing with not-allowed; Python additionally attempts to load "-v1.json" for empty home.
gate_mode=warn with expiry 2027-01-31 leaves a compliance gate non-blocking for a year with no enforcement beyond a ticket string.
`go run ./cmd/pfresidency` recompiles on every fast-tier gate run (120s timeout); build once/cache for latency and offline CI.
config/residency-policy.json's registered owner is "go/backupdrill/region.go" — an unrelated Go file owning the gate's rollout lever is a weak single-writer story.
No test updates asserting language_rule_review or the precheck 45+ gate count, both called out in AC4.
residency_section embeds build-time "validation" output into the canonical manifest — derived, staleable state inside the shipped artifact.
NIT: id-blocks reserved_up_to jumps to 1190, skipping 1187–1189 (gaps permitted, but the block boundary is unexplained).
Template egress.allowed_regions/subprocessors are empty lists while AC1 asks for all six groups "populated".
Every gate run writes engineering/residency-gate.json/.jsonl; confirm gitignore vs. committed-evidence policy to avoid dirty working trees in CI.
SUMMARY: Solid skeleton (explicit home_region, profile-bounded subsets, stable-code intent, warn-first lever, evidence events), but the core AC5 promise — one fixture set proving identical pass/block from both authorities — is missing, and the two validators already disagree (egress group, frequency casing, provider trimming, missing-home handling).
The gate's --report path masks execution/toolchain failures and an unreadable policy silently downgrades to warn, undermining the fail-closed posture this feature exists to establish.

Recommend: land shared conformance fixtures first, close the egress/frequency/missing-home parity gaps, and separate "report" from "non-fatal for policy violations only" before enabling in CI as blocking.
